title: A-linear affine chart coordinates and restriction squares
statement: Let A be a commutative local ring, C its maximal-ideal adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and phi:A to C the structural map. Let U be any open of Spec A, q:Y to U and s:E to Spec C finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and D their supplied completion overlap data [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. Let g:Fin t to A satisfy D(g_j) contained in U. Put V_j=(q followed by U inclusion) inverse-image D(g_j), O=Y times_U the restriction of Spec C to U, and p:O to Y. Equip Gamma(Y), Gamma(E), and Gamma(Y,V_j) with the exact structural A-actions specified in Lean. There exist formal gluing data X for phi and g [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], A-linear coordinate equivalences e:restrict(phi,M prime) to Gamma(E) and d_j:piece(g_j,M_j) to Gamma(Y,V_j), equivalences b_j from C tensor_A M_j to Gamma(O,p inverse-image V_j), and c_ij from (M_j) localized at g_i to Gamma(Y,V_i intersect V_j). Their four numerator equations are: b_j(alpha_j(m prime/1)) is the restriction of D.toCompleted.appTop(e(m prime)); b_j(1 tensor m) is p.app(V_j)(d_j(m)); c_ij(alpha_overlap_ij(m/1)) is the left restriction of d_i(m); c_ij(n/1) is the right restriction of d_j(n). This construction makes no cover or H0 assertion. The coordinate equivalences are A-linear, not merely additive.

proof.text: Since each D(g_j) is contained in U, its inverse image V_j is a finite scheme over an affine scheme, hence is affine. E is affine for the same reason. Set M prime to Gamma(E) with its structural C action and M_j to Gamma(Y,V_j) with the A[1/g_j] action: the image of g_j is invertible on that principal open, so the localization universal property extends the structural A action uniquely. The identity coordinate maps e and d_j are A-linear for precisely the structural actions displayed in the Lean statement.

The double chart V_i intersect V_j is the principal open of the image of g_i in V_j. Mathlib IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen and the module-localization universal property identify its section ring with localize(g_i,M_j); use the underlying equivalence as c_ij. The completed chart is the affine base change of V_j to Spec C. Apply the affine fibre-product tensor formula, including its projection equations, to obtain b_j from C tensor_A M_j to its section ring. The supplied overlapIso, its over equation, and overlap_base identify this same chart with the principal open of g_j in E. Its sections are therefore the localization of M prime at g_j.

Define alpha_j by the E-side principal-localization identification followed by b_j inverse. Define alpha_overlap_ij by the two identifications with sections of V_i intersect V_j. These maps preserve the structural scalar actions; alpha_j preserves C-scalars because overlapIso is over the completed base. On (m/g_j^a)/g_k^b, both cocycle routes restrict m to the triple chart and divide by g_j^a g_k^b. On (m prime/g_i^a)/g_j^b, both square routes restrict the E-section to the completed double chart and divide by g_i^a g_j^b. Swap exchanges these denominators; compare sends (c tensor m)/g_j^b to c tensor (m/g_j^b). Localization uniqueness and additive generation by pure tensors extend the formulas to all inputs. This yields a Data object X.

On a numerator m prime/1 the E-side identification is restriction through D.toCompleted, giving the first equation. The affine tensor projection formula identifies 1 tensor m with p pullback of d_j(m), giving the second. The two localization numerator formulas identify alpha_overlap_ij(m/1) with the left restriction of d_i(m), and n/1 with the right restriction of d_j(n), giving the last two equations. Empty charts have zero sections and zero localizations, so all maps and equations remain valid. For t=0 only the prime module and e remain. No cover assertion, kernel calculation, or H0 characterization is part of this lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_coordinate_squares
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens}
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme} [IsFinite q]
    {E : Scheme.{u}} {s : E ⟶ Spec
      (.of (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A))} [IsFinite s]
    (D : CompletionGluingData A U q E s) (t : ℕ) (g : Fin t → A)
    (hcharts : ∀ j, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g j) ≤ U) :
    let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A
    let φ := algebraMap A C
    let V : Fin t → Y.Opens := fun j ↦ (q ≫ U.ι) ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g j)
    let aY := ((ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ (q ≫ U.ι).appTop).hom
    let aE := ((ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ (s ≫ completionSpecMap A).appTop).hom
    letI : Algebra A Γ(Y, ⊤) := aY.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra A Γ(E, ⊤) := aE.toAlgebra
    letI : ∀ j, Algebra A Γ(Y, V j) := fun j ↦
      ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V j ≤ ⊤)).op).hom.comp aY).toAlgebra
    let O := pullback q (completionSpecMap A ∣_ U)
    let p : O ⟶ Y := pullback.fst q (completionSpecMap A ∣_ U)
    letI : Algebra A C := φ.toAlgebra
    ∃ (X : FormalGlueing.Data.{u, u, u} φ g)
      (e : FormalGlueing.restrict φ X.M' ≃ₗ[A] Γ(E, ⊤))
      (d : ∀ j, FormalGlueing.piece (g j) (X.M j) ≃ₗ[A] Γ(Y, V j))
      (b : ∀ j, FormalGlueing.restrict φ
        (FormalGlueing.extend φ (FormalGlueing.piece (g j) (X.M j))) ≃ Γ(O, p ⁻¹ᵁ V j))
      (c : ∀ i j, FormalGlueing.localize (g i)
        (FormalGlueing.piece (g j) (X.M j)) ≃ Γ(Y, V i ⊓ V j)),
      (∀ j m, b j (X.alpha j (LocalizedModule.mk m 1)) =
        O.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : p ⁻¹ᵁ V j ≤ ⊤)).op
          (D.toCompleted.appTop (e m))) ∧
      (∀ j m, b j (TensorProduct.tmul A (1 : C) m) = p.app (V j) (d j m)) ∧
      (∀ i j m, c i j (X.alpha_overlap i j (LocalizedModule.mk m 1)) =
        Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V i ⊓ V j ≤ V i)).op (d i m)) ∧
      (∀ i j m, c i j (LocalizedModule.mk m 1) =
        Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V i ⊓ V j ≤ V j)).op (d j m))
